These estimated results are used to detect the emergency of the patient.

articleTitle: Implementation of the T-DMB Middleware Platform on the Receiver for Interactive Data services
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we describe the design and implementation of T-DMB middleware which provides receiver platform with a variety of interactive data services based on Java virtual machine, and provides applications with high-level functions such as platform control, broadcast protocol decoding, and application management. We also verify the designed T-DMB middleware through running test of its application on the special purpose T-DMB receiver being done to port it on

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of J2ME And Symbian Applications in Smart Camera Phones
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Nowadays, smart phones have a built-in camera. With their processing capability, we can process captured images, and offer new applications. In this paper we present a performance evaluation of the image processing support in smart phones to answer the question of what we can and we cannot do.

articleTitle: Downlink Transmission Method Applying STBC in S-DMB System Including IMR
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose downlink transmission concept with diversity gain using intermediate module repeater (IMR) in satellite digital multimedia broadcasting (S-DMB) system. We do not regard IMRs as simply repeaters but consider as the antennas for space time block code (STBC) as one of transmit diversity methods. First, a transmission scenario for an application of STBC is represented. And then, we apply STBC in S-DMB system including IMR and compare the performance of the proposed IMR structure to conventional structure. Simulation results show that the transmit diversity gain can definitely be achieved compared to conventional downlink transmission concept in S-DMB system.

articleTitle: (P2-23) A Novel Seamless Vertical Handoff Solution
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this work we propose a seamless vertical handoff solution. We realize the seamless ness by adding a virtual-interface module into current Linux kernel. Different from the mobile-IP based-vertical-handoff systems, there is no need of extra agents or handoff servers in our system. In the experiment, we show that the handoff latency is so short that it is unnoticeable to the applications. Rebuilding transport layer connections is also not required during the period of the handoff. Our system is simple and can be applied to current IP network. Therefore, it is instantly ready for real-world deployment.

articleTitle: Hardware Assisted Pruned Index System For Consumer Electronics
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We describe HAPI, a reconfigurable content indexing device for consumer personal devices such as PDAs and intelligent cell phones, which provides efficient search technology based on a pruned inverted index structure. HAPI accommodates patterns of different lengths to support high reusability and efficiency and can be used either as an internal slave component or as an external co-processor. HAPI controllers take only a minimal percentage of the target device space leaving the majority of the space to term and posting entries.

articleTitle: A MB-OFDM UWB Transmitter for 4-HD Channel Streaming
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The proposed MB-OFDM UWB transmitter system, which is implemented in 0.13 mu CMOS technology, consists of a LPF, a VGA, a V-I converter, an up-mixer, and a driver amplifier. Measured results show maximum transmitted output power level of -10 dBm, output P1dB of -7 dBm, and bandwidth of more than 250 MHz and gain flatness of less than 1 dB for all three sub-bands. The implemented transmitter can transmit 4-HD channel simultaneously, so that make wireless links between multimedia devices demanding high data rate.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Weighting Approach for Image Color and Magnitude Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a classification based weighting approach for color and magnitude interpolation of Bayer pattern CFA (color filter array) image. The simpleness and effectiveness of this approach facilitate the fixed-point implementation of demosizing solution on image processors.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Testing Methods to Determine the RF Performance of Consumer DTV Receiving Appliances
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The author of the paper proposes that the entire range of usable DTV desired signals should be explored, non-invasively to determine the receiver's robustness to interference from first adjacent channel DTV signals, and DTV signals on 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>, 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> adjacent channels with one undesired signal involved. Here the interference mechanism is primarily cross-modulation a form of 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order inter-modulation. In addition, the author proposes tests for true inter-modulation between two undesired DTV signals on those channel pairs known to produce a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order intermodulation product falling in the desired channel.

articleTitle: Highlight Scene Detection And Video Summarization for PVR-Enabled High-Definition Television Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We describe an implementation of our previously developed highlight scene detection and video summarization system, on a PVR-enabled high-definition television system. The implementation poses significant challenges such as consuming minimal computational resources so as to avoid disrupting any of the existing functionalities. The target platform poses challenges such as the absence of a DSP which differ significantly from our previous PVR platform. Our implementation successfully addresses the aforementioned challenges by adapting techniques such as limited buffering and error concealment for dropped frames to the target platform.

articleTitle: 3D Graphics Pipeline Enabled for MPEG2 Decoding
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A novel fixed functionality computing model for synthetic and video image rendering is presented. An OpenGL-ES 1.1 3D graphics pipeline has been used and modified to decode MPEG2 bitstreams ranging from QCIF up to HD resolution achieving drift free quality compared to an MPEG2 decoder output.

articleTitle: A Novel Hierarchical Access Control Scheme in Digital Broadcasting System
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposed the hierarchical access control scheme based on key tree mechanism in digital broadcasting conditional access (CA) system. The proposed scheme optimizes the connection network which is used in the multi-group (MG) scheme (Y. Sun and K.J.R. Liu, 2004). As a result, we archived up to 20% and 9% improvement for a storage and rekey overhead, respectively.

articleTitle: New Challenges to Designers of Digital Terrestrial Television Receivers Concerning Interference
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper examines the interference mechanisms by which signals on first adjacent channels to any DTV channel may cause harmful interference, and how signals on any UHF channel formerly considered to be a UHF taboo channel (and hence left vacant) may cause interference to digital terrestrial television broadcasting (DTTB) reception. Further, the non-linearity of receivers under strong signal conditions from two or more undesired signals on certain pairs of channels can cause interference to reception of signals on two UHF DTV channels.

articleTitle: System-on-a-chip for Portable Audio Player
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The software system for portable devices include audio playback, radio application, audio record, movie playback, image viewer applications. In addition, the portable systems can contain gaming and navigation applications. The portable audio players demand low-power and small form-factors differentiated by wide array of audio effects like equalizer, time scale modification (TSM), and cross-fade. This paper describes the system-on-a-chip (SoC) for portable audio players.

articleTitle: IEEE 1394 Over Coax Bridge for Digital Multimedia Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A 1394-to-coax bridge that enables existing coax infrastructures to be used for connecting IEEE 1394 digital multimedia devices has been developed. The ultra wideband technology is applied to transfer 1394 packets through the coax cable. This paper outlines the architecture and functionality of this bridge node.

articleTitle: Study on adaptive reference picture selection in H.264/AVC interlaced coding
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a reference picture selection scheme in H.264/AVC interlaced coding. Only two reference fields for one B-field are adaptively selected depending on the scene characteristics. The proposed method provides 10% coding efficiency gain over non-adaptive selection methods with the same number of reference pictures.

articleTitle: A Novel TSI application Based on TPEG using T-DMB
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The demand of travel and traffic information (TTI) service has dramatically increased due to rapid increment in the number of vehicles and population of frequently traveling on long weekends. In order to satisfying such a demand, a transport protocol experts group (TPEG) protocol was developed. However, merely two TPEG applications were standardized up to now. This paper presents a novel application, traffic status image information (TSI) application compatible to the existing TPEG protocol, which can be provided in T-DMB network. To verify the stability of TSI protocol, we implemented TSI data server/client, and T-DMB receiver with TSI decoder. Through an experimental broadcasting in the local DMB network, it is shown that the proposed application operates stably and effectively in the verification receiver.

articleTitle: Secure Media Player
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Multimedia content such as music and video is becoming very popular on mobile phones. Most of the content owners prefer to use digital rights management (DRM) technology to protect their copyright. Secure media player (SMP) serves the needs of the content owner by supporting DRM capability. The application described in this paper enables seamless playback of music by integrating high-quality media playback, automatic play list generation, content protection, rights management, content sharing, exporting and intuitive user interfaces, all together.

articleTitle: Implementation of LCD Driver Using Asymmetric Truncation Error Compensation for Mobile DMB Phone Display
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: 16-bit color per pixel to reduce power consumption was generally used for mobile DMB phone display. This would account for the lack of smoothness such as blockings caused by 24-bit to 16-bit asymmetric pixel data truncation. This paper proposes and implements a truncation error compensation algorithm using data expansion from correlated color information for gray scale CCT consistency and for color constancy.

articleTitle: Digest Playback Technology for TV Sports Programs
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Our team of Sanyo has developed an algorithm that efficiently detects highlight scenes of televised sports programs. We limit the detection range of these scenes to their "game section" by applying standard rules of each sport, namely fixed time intervals of certain sports and sound signals of start and end times. Evaluation data suggests this method to be more effective than current conventional models.

articleTitle: Motion Transitive Based Fast Multi-Frame Motion Estimation Algorithm For MPEG-4 AVC/H.264
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The complexity of conducting motion estimation in multiple reference frames is much higher than that of a single reference frame. Generally, we know that temporally neighboring frames have strong correlations with each other. In this paper, the interframe motion correlations are used to estimate motion vectors in multiple reference frames mode efficiently. Our method reuses the pre-coded motion vectors without requiring additional information. The proposed method takes only 23.06% execution time as compared with the approach applying the full search in all the reference frames. Meanwhile, the coding efficiency and visual quality of the proposed method are still comparable to those of the full search.

articleTitle: Blind Watermarking Based on Wavelet Singularity Detection
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present a novel blind watermarking method for copyright protection. Two distance measures are devised to genetically select the significant wavelet singularities for lossless and robust embedding. Then, forward and backward pair checksum generated from the embedded singularities is adopted to alternately correct the attacked image errors for blind retrieval.

articleTitle: Implementation of IEEE 802.11a WLAN Baseband Processor
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presented an implementation of a baseband processor compliant with the IEEE 802.11a standard. Some innovative techniques were proposed to improve performance. For verification and analysis of the design, we used a platform-based SoC design environment. The system consisted of a test-bed for the proposed baseband processor chip and the SoC platform implemented IEEE 802.11a MAC.

articleTitle: A Device for Easily Browsing a Rich Variety of Content Using The Metaphor of Reading Poetry
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose an interface for easily accessing a rich variety of content using the metaphor of reading poetry. The interface is designed for searching content by turning the pages of a book-like device. Using the device, the user can easily access desired content without pressing buttons many times, using complex graphical user interfaces, or using a scroll bar to scroll excessively. The prototype we developed can control TV, radio, media files stored in a HDD, and Internet browsing. The interface can be applied as a controller for commercial products such as PCs, TVs, and HDD recorders.

articleTitle: A Microphone Array Solution for Duplex Hands-Free Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a microphone array solution for speech enhancement in hands-free communication systems. The proposed algorithm aims to enhance a target signal corrupted by background noise as well as the acoustic echo. The main idea lies in the incorporation of both the source and the interference short-term spectral amplitudes in the solution. These spectral components are estimated iteratively to provide a spectrally optimized constraint. Evaluations in a hands-free car environment show that the proposed algorithm is good in suppressing both the noise and the interference even in a double-talk situation.

articleTitle: A Dual QPSK Soft-demapper for ECMA-368 Exploiting Time-Domain Spreading and Guard Interval Diversity
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: When considering the relative fast processing speed and low power requirements for wireless personal area networks (WPAN) and wireless universal serial bus (USB) consumer based products, then the efficiency and cost effectiveness of these products become paramount. This paper presents an improved soft-output QPSK demapper suitable for the products above that not only exploits time diversity and guard carrier diversity, but also merges the demapping and symbol combining functions together to minimize CPU cycles, or memory access dependant upon the chosen implementation architecture. The proposed demapper is presented in the context of multiband OFDM version of UWB (ECMA-368) as the chosen physical implementation for high-rate wireless USB.

articleTitle: Automatic Organization of Digital Photographs
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Media storage devices experience browsing difficulty for users. One cause is the rapid growth in digital photography that results in a large database of stored digital photographs. Managing these photographs manually becomes a complex task. Hence there is a need to organize the digital photographs automatically. The application proposed in this paper solves this by using algorithms for image understanding and techniques for interpreting the metadata present in the digital photographs. Using the algorithms and the metadata, the application organizes the images based on people, event, location and semantic meaning. Hence the application provides an intuitive way for organizing and browsing digital photographs automatically.

articleTitle: An Efficient Design of H.264 Inter Interpolator
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a highly efficient inter interpolation architecture for the H.264/AVC standard is proposed. Since the placement order of frame pixels in the memory is either row-wise or column-wise which may not be suitable for the sample prediction in particular direction, this paper proposes a novel interpolator design which can dynamically configure the datapath for different predicted modes to perform proper computation schedules suitable for the nature input order of reference samples. The proposed design methodology not only can avoid the additional data transposition buffer, but most importantly the communication time spent to move the reference data can be overlapped with the data computation time. Furthermore, by decomposing the chroma interpolation into a series of shift and addition operations, both luma and chroma interpolations can be realized in the same module. Our experimental result shows that our architecture can achieve more than 40% reduction in both processing time and hardware cost. The proposed interpolator can be applied to the dedicated H.264 hardware codec design for various consumer devices.

articleTitle: Perceptual Constraints in Systems for Automatic Music Information Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Perceptual models and data provide useful guidelines in the development of systems for music information retrieval. We show that for music tempo extraction, similarity evaluation, and structure extraction, perceptual data are not only useful in the evaluation of automatic systems but also in their design.

articleTitle: A New Method for Management of Consumers' Private Information on Bidirectional Broadcasting Services
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for management of consumers' private information on bidirectional broadcasting services using IP networks, based on secure distributed RDB (relational database). We also propose a new protocol for browsing user information that was registered in the database from user terminals securely. We compared the processing times to browse user information between the existing usual encryption method and the proposed method. As a result, we can confirm that the latter method is as practical as the former one.

articleTitle: Specific Video Scenes Enlarged and Displayed on Mobile Phone Set
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new system characterizing fighting scenes of Japanese Sumo wrestling on a video stream was built to selectively extract, enlarge, and display them on a display of a mobile phone set. These operations were synchronously queued by the start and stop frames of the fighting scenes.

articleTitle: Pre-equalization Method to Minimize Time Delay of Equalization Digital On-Channel Repeater in ATSC System
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a novel pre-equalization method to minimize the signal processing time delay of the equalization digital on-channel repeater (EDOCR) for the ATSC terrestrial digital TV system. The proposed pre-equalization method is to calculate pre-equalizer filter coefficients by using a baseband signal as a reference signal and a demodulated repeater output signal, then to create new VSB pulse shaping filter coefficients by the convolution of the equi-ripple (ER) filter and the pre-equalizer filter coefficients. The new VSB pulse shaping filter minimizes the time delay of the EDOCR by adjusting the number of its pre-taps and also compensates the linear distortions due to the use of the ER filter and mask filter.

articleTitle: Device Management for Mobile WiMAX Services
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have extended the device management procedures of the open mobile alliance for managing 3G phones to support mobile WiMAX equipment. We use visualization and disconnected operation to produce a cost-effective, maintainable solution which also supports legacy systems.

articleTitle: High-speed Inter-IC Interfacing for Mobile Multimedia Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Distributed processing in today's mobile multimedia devices requires efficient ways of inter-IC communication. This paper presents a hardware block allowing the host IC to have parallel asynchronous access to the resources of the target IC. The block targets mobile multimedia applications. It is composed of an asynchronous logic subsystem, configuration registers, a packer, 4 command/data FIFOs, 3 packer FIFOs, 8 device transaction level (DTL) masters and a DTL slave. The block allows the target IC to be directly connected to a memory controller. The block supports 2D transfers, which improves performance and saves power for mobile video applications.

articleTitle: Data Compression Techniques for Time Codes in Karaoke
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents efficient methods to compress time code aimed at karaoke application by utilizing the linguistic and musical characteristic of karaoke. In particular, we propose a novel codeword rule for the beat of music. Experimental results show that our proposed methods drastically reduce time code.

articleTitle: Efficient Residential Consumer Device Interaction With Network Services
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Consumer access networks are low bandwidth, especially in up-stream direction. This asymmetry is heightened for real-time multimedia applications. The Web wait is not acceptable when in a conversational interface. We describe the use of KPML, a protocol for transporting user stimulus. This paper shows the application of KPML to a typical consumer activity, accessing information sources over the telephone. We include results measuring KPML against other protocols for transporting user stimulus.

articleTitle: A Sequence-Action Recognition Applying State Machine for User Interface
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a novel user interface that recognizes a user's sequence-action to supplement the lacking user interface of mobile devices. To recognize user's various actions (user's gestures and postures) in order of precedence, we used a state machine algorithm. We created mobile games such as fishing and bowling on mobile phones by using this algorithm. The demonstrations show the usability of this state machine for sequence-action recognition.

articleTitle: Object-Based MPEG-4 Authoring Tool for Supporting Sensor Actions and 3D Specifications
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An MPEG-4 scene comprises of various synthetic objects and media data. The scene description includes each object's attributes and behavior. This paper proposes and implements an object-based MPEG-4 authoring tool for supporting sensor actions and 3D specifications, called the O4AT system. The system provides a user-friendly interface and helps the author to create easily an MPEG-4 scene that comprises heterogeneous media objects and related editing sensor actions, and to produce standard MPEG-4 contents with provision of 3D animation presentations. This work hopes to serve as a good reference in the development of MPEG-4 authoring tool systems in Internet and pervasive environments.

articleTitle: Estimating 3D-Shape using fuzzy-neuro logic for a 3-dimensional camera
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose passive methods as a solution to decrease the high cost involved in 3D cameras. The currently available 3-dimensional (3D) cameras are quite expensive because they employ technologies like using three separate lasers to capture XYZ and RGB values, the triangulation method using laser scanner etc. For this purpose, we have developed an approximation technique to calculate depth map for 3D shape recovery. Our algorithm is based on fuzzy-neuro approach. A fuzzy inference system (FIS) is designed and trained using the neural network for the calculation of the depth map. The proposed approximation technique can further be employed in any of the passive methods to acquire depth map for a 3D camera.

articleTitle: Overlapped Semi-parallel LDPC Decoder with Dual-diagonal Structure for WiBro Portable Subscriber Station
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an efficient semi-parallel overlapped LDPC decoding algorithm for WiBro portable subscriber station. We use the dual-diagonal parity matrix structure that the check node update and variable node update can be executed concurrently. With this algorithm, decoding can be completed within 72.2% of clock cycles, compared with non-overlapped decoding.

articleTitle: Service-Oriented Power Management for an Integrated Multi-Function Home Server
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A home server usually is an integrated system of communication, broadcast, game, media center, and home automation. The home server should be turned on for twenty four hours a day because it plays a role of network hub, multimedia contents server, and home automation controller. It is necessary to reduce the power consumption of the home server in order to lower the operational cost. This paper proposes service-oriented power management for a multi-service home server by classifying its resources into small blocks according to the service and supplying power only to the resources needed for the service. We also present some scenarios utilizing this power management.

articleTitle: Mobile reception of Television signals
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. In the 50’s and 60’s when Television reception became common, we found the first TV receivers in vehicles. At that time the analog standards NTSC, PAL and Secam where used. These standards are still used today for terrestrial broadcasting. Television reception was characterized by poor signal reception in terms of picture performance and number of channels received. Different techniques were investigated to improve mobile TV reception.

articleTitle: Auto-Write Strategy System for Optical Disc Recording
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Optical disc recording technology using many types of write strategy (WS) has been developed for optical discs. The optimum WS for each disc is determined based on the material of recordable layer, recording speed, specification of the optical heads and so on. Parameters of WS should be determined by accurate tuning for each optical disc. It has been strongly desired to develop an actual auto-write strategy (AWS) technology to reduce the time for preparing WSs. A new AWS system to optimize the WS for 2x-speed recording on DVD-R discs was developed. This system can detect the pulse widths and signal level of RF signals, and can get better parameters of WS by calculation. As a result, optimum WS can be obtained for optical discs. In this paper, we introduce our new AWS system and experimental result of the effectiveness of this system for the optical discs in the actual market.

articleTitle: Audio Segmentation Assisted Synchronized Lyrics Editing For CE Devices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The facility to add synchronized lyrics to music is not available on any consumer electronics (CE) device. This mechanism though available on a personal computer (PC) through software applications, is not user-friendly. In this paper, we propose a mechanism of introducing an audio segmentation assisted synchronized lyrics editing feature in CE devices. The proposed mechanism takes into consideration the resource-constrained environment of CE devices and the typical end-user sensitivities in operating a CE device.

articleTitle: Adaptive Frame Rate Up-conversion for 3D Graphics Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a novel 3D graphics pipeline for consumer devices able to achieve increased frame-rate at its output, high picture quality, improved temporal anti-aliasing, thanks to a frame-rate up-conversion algorithm based on motion extraction from 3D primitives and efficient compensation, without the need for any motion estimation tool.

articleTitle: Development of Conditional Access system in Terrestrial DMB
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a conditional access system (CAS) that is appropriated in T-DMB and based on an effective multiplexing method for providing a variety of encrypted T-DMB services. The developed CAS in T-DMB is designed to encrypt selected services of all T-DMB services according to the CA modes. Transmitting T-DMB transport stream encrypted by the proposed ensemble multiplexer, we verified their performance by de-scrambling and decoding according to CA mode at the receiver platform.

articleTitle: Peaking Based Chrominance Transient Improvement
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The proposed concept for chrominance sharpness improvement allows operation on high definition signals as well as on standard definition signals respectively on scaled signals up to resolutions of 1920 times 1080. The concept shows dramatically increased noise- and jitter robustness and can avoid artifacts like color overflow and false colors introduced by phase misaligned chrominance components.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Maximal Ratio Combining of Spatially Filtered Signals
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Using multiple receive antennas, some uncorrelated versions of the transmitted signal can be gathered and combined to enhance the system performance. In this case, receive antennas are apart enough to ensure statistically uncorrelated receptions. Whereas, the performance improvement using beamforming antennas usually requires small antenna spacing so that the signals received at from all antennas should be correlated and coherent. This paper discovers and verifies the fact that both beamforming and diversity gains can be simultaneously obtained using array antenna composed of antenna elements linearly spaced out half-wavelength.

articleTitle: A 192MHz to1.946GHz Programmable DLL-Based Frequency Multiplier for RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A delay-locked loop based frequency multiplier is presented using tsmc 0.18 mum CMOS process parameters. The multiplication factor N can be chosen as an integral number whereas the output frequency range is from 192 MHz to 1.946 GHz. The total power consumption is less than 5.8 mW with a 1.8 V supply. The locking time of the DLL core is 0.66 mus at 250 MHz. The cycle-to-cycle jitter of the DLL core is 46 ps.

articleTitle: DFT-based Carrier Recovery for Satellite DVB Receivers
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A non-data-aided carrier recovery algorithm suitable for satellite digital video broadcasting receivers is presented, which can counteract large carrier offsets at signal-to-noise ratio as low as 3dB. The proposed two-step scheme consists of low-resolution discrete Fourier transform (DFT) to acquire coarse carrier frequency offset, and carrier recovery loop for fine frequency offsets tracking. Simulation results are given to demonstrate the capability of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Historical overview of Equalization in Consumer Electronics
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In the 1970s, the remaining picture quality limitations were concentrated in the transmission path, with multipath reflections the most challenging. Laboratory techniques to cancel the ghost images had surprisingly little benefit. What remained after substantial ghost reduction was still objectionable, unable to justify the high cost of the circuits. Simultaneously, the cable industry was rapidly penetrating the market, leaving few ghosts to cancel. So the effort was abandoned. Years later, interest in equalization again arose to aid transmitting data in the vertical blanking interval. In the digital environment, if the signal is improved sufficiently to distinguish "1s" from "0s", the data recovery could be near perfect. Unfortunately, teletext did not enjoy market acceptance in the US. Later, equalization became essential to the success of broadcast digital television. Currently, the excitement over mobile and portable applications promises to finally make equalization both mandatory and ubiquitous.

articleTitle: The Conversion of a Device And a Control Message in The Universal Middleware Bridge
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes how the conversion of a device and a control message is accomplished in a UMB. The UMB solves interoperability problems caused by the heterogeneity of several types of home network middleware. To solve the problems, conversion of a device and messages among the middleware is indispensable. Devices can see and control other devices connected to different middlewares in the UMB framework by the mechanism of device and message conversion.

articleTitle: Bidirectional DFE Arbitrated by Viterbi Decoder Path Metrics
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A bidirectional decision feedback equalizer (DFE) is proposed with the arbitration of the Viterbi decoder. The proposed DFE uses the minimum path metric between Viterbi decoders for the forward and reverse DFEs in the arbitration process. It has over 2 dB SNR gain against the conventional bidirectional DFE and the single DFE.

articleTitle: Memory Management Circuit for The Next Generation Optical Drives
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a memory management circuit, we call memory manager, implemented in a single chip controller used for all the media of Blu-ray, DVD and CD. The memory manager has a hierarchy structure to realize memory mapping and bus control for each media, and also has bus occupation time control function to realize the operation at the maximum speed for Blu-ray. We have confirmed the expected performance by the simulation and evaluation on the actual drive system.

articleTitle: An analysis of Hierarchical APSK and PSK scheme and an Application to increase the transmission capacity of the S-DMB
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper analyzes the optimal changes in the modulation mode according to the error rate margin and power margin of the present system of the hierarchical modulation system. The aim of the research is to increase the capacity of the digital multimedia broadcasting via satellite (S-DMB) or other systems.

articleTitle: Deployment Strategy And Performance Evaluation of The IPv6 Home Network Using The Home Server
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The IPv6 is an inevitable technology for the ubiquitous home network due to the increasing numbers of the consumer electronics (CEs) and the explosive demands for the home network services which requires end-to-end connectivity through the Internet. In order to provide services based on the IPv6 in the home network, the home-to-home tunneling and IPv4/6 transition mechanisms are required due to the late deployment of the IPv6 in the public network. The paper proposes a deployment strategy and evaluates the performances of the IPv6 home network on the test-bed using the home server, which establishes connections between CEs and the Internet. Additionally the paper also proposes a novel IPv4/6 transition mechanism (proxy ARP/NDP for NAT-PT) to support interoperability among various IPv4/6 based CEs within a home network.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Quality Enhancement Method for Binaural Cue Coding - A Hiss Reduction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Parametric spatial audio coding (PSAC) is a promising method which compresses multi-channel signals to extremely compact backward compatible representations. However, some implementations (e.g. BCC) usually have noise on their output audio signals and thus degrade their listening qualities. In this paper, a low complexity quality enhancement method is presented.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a High-Speed Descrambling Engine for Multi-stream CableCARD
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we have present a hardware design of the high-speed descrambling engine for supporting multi channels in multi-stream cableCARD. The designed descrambling engine has been implemented on a FPGA. The presented design has a parallel processing structure that is extendable according to required input bandwidth. Especially we have verified that designed descrambling engine supported up to 200 Mbps input bandwidth.

articleTitle: Color Refinement for Natural Scene Images
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new method for selective color refinement of natural scene images is proposed. It aims to perform a post processing visual improvement of selected chromatic classes. This application is suitable for consumer devices, where either physical or computational constraints lead to obtain poor color rendition. The proposed solution improves the accuracy of color reproduction for three selected chromatic classes, i.e. skin, vegetation, sky, which have the most impact on the human visual system. The entire process is carried out in a cost effective way, by an automatic chromatic classifier driven by an accurate statistic characterization of a large image database, followed by an adaptive and intensity preserving color enhancement process. Many consumer applications can take advantage from this approach: digital still cameras, color display drivers and other color reproduction systems.

articleTitle: Accurate Reconstruction of Non-rigid 3D Shapes
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The aim of this paper is to create an accurate 3D-TV contents from 2D-video which can be used in a commercial 3D-TV broadcast environment. In this paper we propose an accurate recovering of non-rigid 3D shapes using a chained partial rigid factorization method. We have extended the existing rigid factorization algorithm to the stereo camera case. Our focus in this paper is on estimating deformable shapes from stereo images. Our experiments show the improved results for reconstructions.

articleTitle: Networked Device Capability And Content Media Format Matching Scheme For Multimedia Access
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a scheme to dynamically match capabilities of content sinks and media formats of items supplied by content sources to improve interoperability among a wider range of networked CE devices. The scheme proposes the use of transcoders located in external networks (e.g. Internet) when a match is not found locally. Here "media format" refers to the combination of content encoding format and packaging or transport method used to make available the content item on the network. Existing capability matching methods rely on standard repositories agreed a priori such as MIME (multipurpose Internet mail extensions) media types, and DLNA (Digital Living Network Alliance) media format profiles. The proposed scheme based on external transcoders enables future support of new profiles based on newly invented formats or new combinations of existing formats and packaging or transport methods. This extensible approach makes possible rendering of content items available in media profiles unknown to the renderer. Our capability matching scheme improves media interoperability when compared with existing methods.

articleTitle: A Low Power QXGA Camera Signal Processor for Mobile Camera Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a low power and high performance camera signal processor system-on-a-chip (SoC) architecture for mobile camera applications such as the mobile phone, the personal digital assistant (PDA), and the personal multimedia player (PMP). In this work, we presented the use of the gated clock approach to reduce power consumption. The area of this chip is 2.8 mm times 2.7 mm and it was fabricated with the 0.18-mum CMOS process. This device packaged with flash memory in a multi-chip package (MCP) technology and dissipates 76 mW at 1.8 V/50 MHz.

articleTitle: A New Audio Signal Analyzer using PCA and MGD
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new audio signal analyzer. Since our system can represent the possibility that the audio signal belongs to some audio classes, such as speech and music, it can be useful for several applications, such as audiovisual indexing and retrieval system.

articleTitle: Transmitter Pre-emphasis and Adaptive Receiver Equalization for Duobinary Signaling in Backplane Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive equalization technique of a multi-gigabit channel using duobinary signaling is proposed. Both the receiver and transmitter are equalized and implemented using ADS. The results show that the duobinary signaling performs better than NRZ at half of the bandwidth. The algorithm was tested in a Tyco XAUI-FR4 backplane.

articleTitle: Post-Processing Noise Suppressor with Adaptive Gain-Flooring for Cell-Phone Handsets and IC Recorders
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a post-processing noise suppressor with adaptive gain-flooring. By controlling gain-flooring based on voice activity and an output-SNR, distortion of the enhanced speech is reduced with natural transition between a speech and a non-speech section. Subjective evaluation results, with a preprocessing noise suppressor, a codec and a post-processing noise suppressor connected in tandem, show that the post-processing noise suppressor improves the five-grade mean opinion score by as much as 0.5 when suppression by the preprocessing noise suppressor is insufficient. The proposed post-processing noise suppressor is promising for the receiver in cell-phone handsets and IC recorders.

articleTitle: Interactive Object Extraction/Removal System for Digital Camera
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present an interactive object extraction/removal system for digital image. The proposed system includes two functions: object extraction and object removal. The user can employ this system to separate the target object from background (object extraction) or remove it from background with filled region (object removal).

articleTitle: A Memory Compression Method for Avoiding Perceivable Distortion Due to Intra-Prediction in H.264 Decoders
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper analyzes the video-quality degradation mechanism in an H.264 decoder with memory compression and proposes a new DPCM memory compression method which avoids that degradation. When memory compression methods used in MPEG-2 decoders are applied to H.264 decoders, heavy degradation sometimes occurs because H.264 employs directional spatial prediction in intra-coding. The proposed method avoids such degradation by deploying DPCM base points to intra reference pixels in order to protect them from compression distortion. Simulation results show that the proposed method significantly improves video-quality, in the best case by 7.51 dB in PSNR, over that of conventional methods, and subjective quality is also improved.

articleTitle: Preamble Based OFDM Timing Synchronization Method for WLAN And WMAN Standard Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel timing synchronization method for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. Conventional OFDM timing synchronization methods require their uniquely designed preamble structures to improve the accuracy of timing synchronization. However, proposed method can be used to most OFDM systems independently of their preamble structures.

articleTitle: Detecting digital forgeries using of a lighting direction
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for digital forensic using a technique to detect a lighting direction. We describe how the estimated the lighting direction from a segmented image and show a ratio of detecting forgery.

articleTitle: Biometric Template Protection: A Key-Mixed Template Approach
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents key-mixed template (KMT), which mixes a user's template with a secret key to generate another form of template, to prevent the biometric template stored in the database from back end attack, snooping, and tampering attack.

articleTitle: A Proposal of Automotive Anticollision Radars Based on Spread Spectrum Techniques
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The use of automotive collision warning radars for improving the road safety is a well recognized opportunity, and a lot of proposals have been already evaluated, in theory and practice. In this paper we present an approach based on the classic direct sequence spread spectrum method, where the pseudo noise sequences consist of gold codes or chaotic signals. By exploiting the degrees of freedom they offer, in conjunction with their good correlation properties, chaotic signals are potentially able to improve the system efficiency compared with gold codes, by increasing the radar detection capability.

articleTitle: Adaptive Channel Equalizer for Wireless Access in Vehicular Environments
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Dedicated short range communication (DSRC) is the key component in intelligent transportation systems (ITS). The goal of this technology is to help driver and passengers getting multimedia services via wireless communication equipment during the movement of vehicle, so as to improve the traffic safety and enhance the transportation efficiency. The paper is focus on the DSRC baseband technical analysis and the application development. Based on the WLAN 802.11a architecture, we develop a new adaptive channel estimation algorithm that uses two kinds of feedback tracking and pilot aid to enhance wireless access ability in vehicular environments.

articleTitle: Low Compexity Motion Analysis for Mobile Video Devices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a low-complexity method for estimation of translational motion in video sequences, based on the principle that 2D image translation results in translation of image projections. The method uses a single pixel-by-pixel frame scan to extract a compact frame-descriptor. The translation between frames is determined by matching frame-descriptors using fixed-point implementation of the phase correlation method (PCM). The method gives reliable results even when video images are blurred by significant and rapid motion and in the presence of independent local motions. Real-time performance has been achieved in a low-cost DSP board.

articleTitle: Efficient Validation/Verification of a Robust DVB-H Link Layer
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Currently, various semiconductor manufacturers develop silicon solutions for DVB-H receivers. One of the key functions in a DVB-H receiver is the link layer. In order to differentiate, manufacturers can choose between basic or advanced link-layer implementation concepts, resulting in modest or excellent performance. This paper presents the required validation and verification tools for evaluating the DVB-H link-layer robustness, capable of generating and analyzing extreme signal conditions. Furthermore, we also discuss an advanced analysis tool required to inspect the output IP-based data, service information and program specific information of the link layer. The earlier simulation results for improved link-layer performance presented by the tools are validated from a newly developed silicon implementation.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-function Audio System in Bedrooms
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents design of a multi-function audio system in bedrooms. The proposed system can be installed on traditional headboards, thus has potential benefits in retrofit, convenience, and is unobtrusive. The system serves to play audio in bedrooms, can be used as a hands-free telephone system, and also provides a non invasive noise reduction system. Although the noise reduction system is capable of reducing environmental noises emanating from home appliances, real-time experiments were performed to show the capabilities of the system in reducing the more annoying snore noise. A modified twin-size headboard was used to perform experiments. Results of noise cancellation experiments with snore noise indicate a reasonable size of quiet zone with satisfactory performance achieved with the proposed low-cost system.

articleTitle: Development of QoS-aware Ubiquitous Content Access Testbed
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a testbed of QoS-aware ubiquitous content access (UCA), which allows a user to access and consume multimedia content through convergent networks of broadcasting and communications (WLAN/CDMA) using diverse devices in a seamless and transparent way, is designed and implemented based on the adaptation of scalable and non-scalable content.

articleTitle: A low complexity TV remote controller with user individual behavior embedded
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper has discussed a low complexity channel recommendation system on TV remote controller, which aims to, with limited processing speed and memory capacity, recommend interesting channels to viewers in various time intervals according to different preferences and habits. This system comprises two important parts: "three-dimensional bitmap for user behavior" and "channel-reference-bits algorithm". "Three-dimensional bitmap for user behavior" is used to record the behavior mode of watching TV and storage mode of preference data in a three-dimensional data space, while "channel-viewed-bits algorithm" is used to screen habitual channels of viewers from stored data.

articleTitle: Improved Edge-adaptive Demosaicking Method for Artifact Suppression around Line Edges
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present an edge-adaptive demosaicking method with artifact suppression. Although various demosaicking methods have been proposed, they still suffer from artifacts around line edges. In order to suppress such undesirable artifacts around line edges, the proposed method first determines line edge patterns and interpolates missing pixels along detected directions. Then, refinement and calibration processes are carried out in series to improve the quality of reconstructed images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method produces visually pleasing images and outperforms existing demosaicking methods in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR).

articleTitle: Dynamic Difficulty Controlling Game System
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes how we can control the level of difficulty in a game based on a user's skill. In order to solve this problem, we propose dynamic difficulty controlling game system (DDCGS). We use modified genetic algorithm and factor of difficulty control in a game (FDC) as chromosomes and factor of user's adaptation to a game (FUA) as fitness in the genetic algorithm. Then we prove propriety of DDCGS in our experiments and conclusion.

articleTitle: Transcoding Selectively Encrypted H.264 Bitstreams
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a novel secure transcoding scheme with H.264 compression, whereby only selected parts of the bitstream are encrypted to allow transcoding without decryption. Security comparisons are carried out for three schemes where encryption is applied to only the I frames, DC coefficients or motion vectors. I frame encryption, which provides the best security of the three schemes, is combined with two different transcoding architectures. Simulation results, on the 'Foreman' dataset show a significant performance enhancement in both systems, demonstrating their potential in consumer oriented commercial applications.

articleTitle: Massive Stripe Cache And Prefetching for Massive File I/O
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a massive stripe prefetching (MSP) scheme on a massive stripe cache (MSC) structure, which has been implemented in a Linux kernel. Our schemes efficiently perform on massive files such as audio/video files and a bulk of small files. MSC exploits spatial locality. MSP discriminates metadata reads and contiguous data reads in the stripe level, thereby boosting the read performance independently of a file-based prefetching.

articleTitle: Implementation of an All-digital Receiver for WDM/SCM-PON Subscriber Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Wavelength division multiplexing/sub-carrier multiplexing-passive optical network (WDM/SCM-PON) is the most flexible and cost-effective technique to transmit multimedia signals with varied formats and speeds. In this paper we propose an all-digital receiver structure supporting up to high bit rate of 120 Mbps for a WDM/SCM-PON subscriber network. The proposed receiver is implemented on a single-chip FPGA and its performance is verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: A New Image-stabilizing Method by Transferring Electric Charges
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a new image stabilization method that utilizes electric charge transfer in the vertical transfer register of a CCD image sensor. This method repeats a series of actions including one or more continuous exposures according to the degree of camera shake, transferring and adding electric charges in the vertical transfer register to correct image blurs. Since this technique does not require mechanical components, external memory or digital image processing circuits, it allows cameras to be miniaturized and costs reduced.

articleTitle: Improving TCP/IP Performance over Last-hop Wireless Networks for Streaming Video Delivery
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper discusses a protocol for delivery of streaming video with a short play-out deadline over a last-hop wireless network, which trades reliability for latency. This protocol could be implemented in the wireless access point to improve the quality of the received streaming video over an Internet connection to an office or home. The main ideas of the protocols are two-fold: 1) across the wireless link: perform local retransmissions and drop any stale packets; 2) across the entire source-destination path: hide duplicated acknowledgements from the sender to avoid retransmissions. In addition, the protocol takes advantage of application level framing and acknowledges missing transport layer segments with expired play-out deadlines. Although several existing protocols partially solve the problem of streaming video delivery in this particular context, either by improving the performance of the wireless link or by dropping the stale packets, to our best knowledge none of the protocols solves the complete problem. The performance of our protocol is compared against the performance of the snoop, TCP RTM, combined with snoop and TCP RTM protocols, as well as TCP Reno. The results of simulations show a manyfold improvement of the goodput across a wide range of packet-error rates.

articleTitle: An Efficient Password-Based E-mail Protocol for Encrypted E-mail Transmissions on Mobile Equipment
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an efficient e-mail protocol that can be used for secure e-mail transmissions between mobile equipments, especially mobile phones equipped with IC (integrated circuit) chips. The protocol makes it possible that a user who has a mobile phone, but has no public-key certificate, sends or receives an encrypted e-mail using a memorable password shared with his mobile e-mail server only. Therefore the protocol can be more easily implemented and efficiently used for mobile e-mail systems. To the best of our knowledge, the new protocol is the first e-mail protocol does not require expensive public-key certificate related computations.

articleTitle: Low-cost handling of combing artifacts in motion-compensated deinterlacing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new method to improve the combination of the motion-compensated field with the original field in deinterlacing applications. It is based on the direct detection of combing artifacts and on a new measurement for the vector reliability.

articleTitle: Using Cryptography as Copyright Protection for Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Copyright protection should not be limited to content alone. Software, running on an embedded device and stored in its flash-ROM, is also in danger of being copied or rebranded, resulting in lost revenues and liability issues. Cryptography is a way to prevent this, while being invisible to the customers.

articleTitle: A Fast Motion Estimation Algorithm Based on The Direction of Motion Vectors
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper suggests a simple scheme in which the predicted motion vector is calculated using the spatio-temporal neighborhood information. The predicted motion vector is chosen as initial search center. The search pattern can be divided into 4 or 8 sectors based on the direction of the predicted motion vector. This predictive search center is found closer to the global minimum. The final sector based search pattern is adaptive as it is direction based and hence significantly reduces the computational complexity. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has good predicted image quality and less computational complexity as compared to other approaches.

articleTitle: Design of Protocol Adaptation Layer for IEEE 1394 over IEEE 802.15.3
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, protocol adaptation layer for IEEE 1394 over IEEE 802.15.3 was designed. Connection procedure method between coordinator and slave device and cycle time synchronization method between wired IEEE 1394 device and wireless device were presented. If new method is adopted for various wireless 1394 products, consumer electronics devices such as DTV and set-top box or PC devices on a 1394 bus network can transmit real time data to the AV devices on the other 1394 bus in a different place via IEEE 802.15.3.

articleTitle: Multi-Protocol WiMedia UWB Radio Platform implemented in Single-Chip CMOS
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We are building single chip CMOS solutions which implement the WiMedia ultrawideband radio standard. This includes a WiMedia compliant radio (PHY), baseband, medium access controller (MAC), a processor, memory and standard I/O interfaces. Firmware can be loaded into the processor so that the device can support Bluetooth 3.0, WiNet (Internet protocols), and certified wireless USB.

articleTitle: A Congestion Control Algorithm in IEEE 802.11 Wireless LAN for Throughput Enhancements
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a congestion control algorithm, which uses cross-layered approach and rate-based transmission, for IEEE 802.11 wireless LANs (WLANs). The proposed algorithm considers the contention density which represents the degree of contention level experienced at a given station. From the contention density, each station can compute available bandwidth and adjusts its sending rate. The evaluation results show that throughput achieved by our algorithm is around 10% and about 20% at peak point, higher than that of TCP and TCP-SACK.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Coarse Frequency Acquisition in IEEE 802.11 a
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A novel coarse carrier frequency estimation algorithm is proposed for IEEE 802.11a receivers. This method employs the properties of the preamble to reduce the carrier acquisition problem to single tone frequency estimation. It offers good performance in both AWGN and multipath channels, especially at low SNR.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of PO-THMA UWB System Using Mutually Orthogonal MHP Pulses
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a pulse order time-hopping multiple-access ultra wideband (PO-THMA UWB) system using modified Hermite polynomial (MHP) pulses. The MHP pulses have the orthogonal property between different ordered pulses, and that property makes the THMA UWB system have increased transmission capacity. We derived the bit error rate (BER) of the proposed system theoretically, and also show that the BER performance and capacity are improved dramatically compared with the THMA system only.

articleTitle: Semantic Photo Album Based on MPEG-4 Compatible Application Format
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a promising photo album system that enables augmented use of digital photos over a wide range of multimedia devices and semantic consumption of photos as well. The proposed system contains an album engine to create metadata and a photo player to consume the photos. It operates based on a standardized application format to encode a group of photos and associated metadata. Experiments showed that the proposed system achieved reasonable albuming performance.

articleTitle: Signal-based Music Searching and Browsing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes an approach to the problem of finding songs in some sense similar to a query song. This is a problem of increasing importance, because consumers owning large digital music collections wish to navigate these and to add new songs by searching on-line. The technological approach is described, leading to the description of a simple demonstrator.

articleTitle: Complexity-Constrained Feature Selection for Classification
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Continuous monitoring of audio-visual context on mobile devices requires algorithms with gentle demands on computational resources. Existing feature selection strategies for classification do not account for the complexity associated with feature extraction. We present a complexity-constrained feature selection algorithm that is independent of the classifier architecture and demonstrate that it leads to superior feature sets if the allowed computational complexity is limited.

articleTitle: A Fast Intra-Mode Decision Algorithm for P-Slices in H.264/AVC Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: H.264/AVC video coding has significantly improved video compression performance compared to other video coding schemes by using a variable block size and a rate-distortion optimization (RDO) technique for each macro-block. As a result, the complexity and computational load have been significantly increased, causing many difficulties for use in real-time applications. A fast intra-mode decision algorithm is proposed for reduction video compression complexity that uses an inter-mode block type for fast intra-prediction. The inter-best mode block type and the direction of the texture edge or object boundary are highly correlated at the inter-mode decision. Based on inter-best mode information, only a small number of intra-prediction modes are used. Experimental results show that this scheme can significantly improve the speed of the intra-mode search procedure with a negligible loss in the peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) and a minimal bit rate increase.

articleTitle: Theorems And Algorithms for People Tracking, Posture Analysis And Activity Recognition Using 2D Distance Sensors
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Human activity recognition should be the key technology that lets computer interact with people and bring them into an intellectual, secure and comfortable life style. In this digest, we propose an alternative method using two-dimensional distance sensors to track people, analyze their postures, and recognize their activities based on the proposed theorems and algorithms.

articleTitle: Biometric Access Control for Digital Media Streams in Home Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Methods for controlling access to digital media content in the home environment using biometric sensing techniques are described. A wireless rebroadcast system for IP-TV content was retrofitted with a combination of fingerprint authentication and face recognition modules. Family members are enrolled and new individuals may be added to the system by a master user. Access to content requires fingerprint based authentication from a wireless PDA and the system also checks dynamically if it can recognize enrolled uses amongst those "sitting on the couch".

articleTitle: Providing Web Services over DVB-H: Mobile Virtual Web Services
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we introduce our experiences in accessing Web Services (WS) from DVB-H terminals. As client should be as simple as possible, we propose to move its complexity to the DVB-H provider by defining virtual WS. Because of this visualization, the DVB-H provider makes the mobile client independent of the service location or availability and even makes the client QoS-aware.

articleTitle: Sort Middle Pipeline Architecture for Efficient 3D Rendering
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a high performance fixed function 3D graphics pipeline based on sort-middle computing paradigm. The proposed architecture implements the full specification of the OpenGL|ES 1.1 open standard and is specifically designed for a cost effective integration on consumer devices, in particular on low-power mobile ones.

articleTitle: A System Design for Residential Services Delivery Over Internet
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A system providing Internet remote access of residential services has been developed. The system allows users to access their residential services, e.g. appliance control, under the constraint that the residential gateways (residential clients) are connected to the Internet through an unpredictable or an intranet IP address. Security schemes are provided for the connections between residential clients and remote clients. The system allows the user to access their residential services confidentially.

articleTitle: Design of Health-Care Home Gateway (HCHG) over Digital Cable Television Network
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a heath-care home gateway (HCHG), with the abilities of wireless transmission by using a ZigBee module and multimedia home platform (MHP), over digital cable television (CATV) network. By means of HCHG, it is mainly to transmit the vital signs of the CATV subscribers via digital CATV network to the medical/health-care center, and could further to consult their health condition with the professional medical and nursing personnel timely.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Front-End System for BD/DVD/CD Recorder
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper introduces a reconfigurable front-end system that consists of a RF chip and two data processors (DPs). The system has capability of reading BD/DVD/CD and recording BD/DVD. It can be implemented with a RF chip and a BD DP for only BD mode and combined with a RF chip and a DVD/CD DP for only DVD/CD. The algorithms for improving playability and recordability of BD are developed and implemented. The system is fully verified with all kinds of real BD/DVD/CD. A RF chip is fabricated in 0.65 mum Bi-CMOS process technology and two DPs are in 0.18 mum CMOS.

articleTitle: A Software Wireless Streaming Architecture Supporting telematics device
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We describe the design and implementation of mobile streaming middleware support for wireless disconnection integrity on embedded operating system. The key technologies include functionally clustering of executable codes, pre-fetch map creation to reference transferring, and event monitoring to rollback event committing a failure.

articleTitle: On WiMAX Performance with Multiple Antenna Transmission
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we aim to investigate the performance of employing several transmit and receive antennas in WiMAX in order to improve the system performance. WiMAX is a wireless technology that provides broadband data at rates over 3 bits/second/Hz. In this paper we will consider multiple antenna techniques that do not require channel knowledge, i.e space-time block coding (STBC), receiver diversity and cyclic delay diversity. The performance results show that STBC and cyclic delay diversity is superior but to an expense in complexity.

articleTitle: Playback Synchronization Techniques for Networked Home Appliances
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of device synchronization, particularly as it manifests on wireless home networks. Basic clock synchronization can be achieved between two independent devices over a packet network using the network time protocol (NTP). However, as the D/A stages of the two devices may introduce additional clock skew more sophisticated approaches are required to achieve the necessary level of device synchronization for high quality playback of audio data. Practical applications in the fields of VOIP telephony and audiophile quality speaker synchronization are discussed.

articleTitle: A Layered Space-Time-Frequency Coded OFDM for Next Generation Mobile Multimedia Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We consider the architecture of layered space-time-frequency (STF) coding as a combination of orthogonal precoding and hybrid space-time block coding (STBC) for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless multimedia systems. This approach provides both maximum transmit diversity and spatial multiplexing with moderate complexity. The proposed layered STF coded transmission scheme is practical and efficient over multipath fading channels. In addition, it is possible to obtain maximum frequency diversity gain by means of the orthogonal precoding that enhances the system performance.

articleTitle: Detection of Music Segment Boundaries using Audio-Visual Features for a Personal Video Recorder
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have extended our sports video browsing framework for personal video recorders, such as recordable-DVD recorders, blu-ray disc recorders and/or hard disc recorders, to music segment detection. Our extension to Japanese broadcast music video programs consists of detecting audio segment boundaries such as conversations with guests followed by music/song etc. Our proposed system first identifies the music/song scenes using audio analysis, and then adjusts the start/end position by detecting video shot changes, so as to achieve accurate detection of the music segment thus enabling rapid browsing. Our preliminary results indicate that our audio-only summarization with scene change support works well for music video content. We can therefore integrate the enhancement into our product at a low computational cost.

articleTitle: A Personal Video Recording System Using H.264 and MPEG-2 Transport Stream
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This article describes a personal video recorder (PVR) system that uses H.264 for video coding and MPEG-2 transport stream as data format for simultaneous record and playback. Using H.264 provides two times longer recording time over MPEG-2 based on the same video quality. The 2004 amendment of the MPEG-2 system standard added support for the transport of none MPEG-2 AVC video data using MPEG-2 transport stream.
