This article discusses the overall architecture of the PVR and several key technical aspects of the implementation, including A/V capture, synchronization, storage and play-back. The implementation uses the Davinci digital video software development kit (DVSDK).

articleTitle: Impacts of Repetitions and Segment Size Variability on Object-Level Throughput in T-DMB
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Data services in terrestrial-digital multimedia broadcasting (T-DMB) inherently have the disadvantage of retransmitting data unnecessarily for reliability. This paper proposes a novel optimized transmission policy using segment size and repetition number variability, which maximizes the object-level throughput. The theoretical modeling and simulation results demonstrate that our policy provides a throughput gain over the conventional protocol.

articleTitle: Optimized Servo System of DVD Drive for Video Camera
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the servo system to suppress the influence of vibration for built-in DVD drive inside a video camera. The developed servo system prevents tracking disturbance caused by vibration acceleration and focus disturbance caused by disc trembling due to Coriolis effect.

articleTitle: Error Concealment for 3G-324M Mobile Videophones Over a WCDMA networks
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Compressed video bitstreams are intended for real-time transmission over communication networks. Because video coding standards eliminate the temporal, spatial, and statistical redundancies, the coded video bitstreams are very sensitive to transmission errors. Many error resilience coding schemes are available to get high video quality over noisy channels. We propose an error resilient coding technique to limit the effect of error propagation in low bit-rate video coding. The success of error resilient coding techniques relies on how accurately the transmission errors can be detected. Therefore, we propose a very simple error detection technique using data hiding. After error detection, we conceal the corrupted MB data using intra MB refresh and motion compensation with the estimated motion vector. This method will be useful in video communication in error prone environment such as WCDMA networks.

articleTitle: Enabling Introduction of Stereoscopic (3D) Video: Compression Standards & its Impact on Display Rendering
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Since the introduction of TV, major new steps have been color- and high definition (HD) TV. The next expected milestone is stereoscopic (3D) TV. Important ingredients are availability of suitable 3D displays, practical content generation and compression standards to carry the 3D signals.

articleTitle: Design of Memory Sub-System in H.264/AVC Decoder
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present the memory sub-system of a H.264/AVC decoder designed for high profile and level 4. Our design incorporates a synchronization buffer as a pre-cache buffer. We investigate the efficiency of DRAM access and power dissipation when the buffer is designed at different granularities. Statistical results show that the granularity of larger block size has higher memory efficiency, less access cycles and power dissipation. However, the granularity of 8times8 block size provides better trade-off among cost, efficiency, power, and real-time requirement.

articleTitle: Transmission Loss And Radiated Electric Field Characteristics of Transmission Medium for Ubiquitous Network
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Transmission loss and radiated electric field characteristics of the pipe-based transmission line as new transmission medium are calculated by using the method of moment, and it is clear that the calculated values almost agreed with measured values. In addition, it is confirmed that the pipe based transmission system can obtain dynamic range of about 56 dB and realize secure transmission, even if the radiated electric field from the pipe-based transmission line comply with the limit of the information technology equipment specified by VCCI.

articleTitle: Real-Time Demosaicking for Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present an effective and efficient demosaicking algorithm for natural images. A new reciprocal table accurately estimates the relation between edges and gradient weights, and it achieves regular, succinct, and fast operations with excellent performance. Flexible and optional procedures adapt to different constraints on embedded systems. Our proposed method has 10.94 dB, 9.14 dB, and 9.05 dB improvements over bilinear method in red, green, and blue channels respectively. In visual results, the reconstructed images have smooth artifact. The performance is very close to recent methods, still superiorly.

articleTitle: Robust HD Video Stream Transmission for Wireless DTV
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper the authors describe a clock synchronization system with buffer management mechanism that enables "TV adoptable quality" of HD (high definition) video transmission via wireless network. Like DLNA (digital living network alliance), the usage of IP based network for CE devices, especially for audio video appliance, is increasing its importance. Unlike for IT technology based devices such as PC, consumers expect CE devices to provide more stable functions to enjoy audio visual contents than what they are experiencing with Internet streaming. They expect it even with HD video contents. Based on well considered simulation for wireless network usage at home, the buffering system that authors describe here can offer the certain quality of service with HD video transmission to CE oriented customers.

articleTitle: Dynamic User Interface Update Using Web Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an advanced UI framework for dynamic updating a web page during UI interaction on the local networks and over Internet. Current existing Web technologies have a difficulty in updating user interface without refreshing the page when server needs to send information related to the change of status or event. Thus, the proposed management of remote UI framework suggests new robust and dynamic UI update mechanisms.

articleTitle: Blu-ray Disc 6x read/write control LSI with an adaptive PRML detector
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A 6times-speed BD and all DVD/CD read/write control LSI has been developed. It contains a PRML detector that adopts an adaptive equalizer and an adaptive Viterbi decoder to improve playback performance. As a result of BER measurements, a large margin sufficient for playing back 6times BD was obtained.

articleTitle: Wrapping TV Interface for Watching Multiple Programs Efficiently
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We developed a TV browser user-interface called "wrapping interface" with clip and paste manners for watching multiple programs efficiently. We studied operations based on the concept of the wrapping interface and developed several prototypes, and we discussed additional ideas for enhancing the wrapping interface.

articleTitle: High-speed Recording in Blu-ray Disc Drive
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The read/write performance at 4times-speed for BD drive system was investigated. The criteria of residual error and write strategy suitable for 4times recording were found. Then, a prototype drive proved 4times recording with sufficient low jitter value.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Color Adjustment for Mobile Application Displays with a Skin Protection Algorithm on a CIE1931 Diagram
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Most mobile application displays use LCDs (liquid crystal displays). Such panels have various problems, including decreases in transmission and saturation. We propose an algorithm to solve these problems by using data processing without panel replacement. In general, the subtle problems in color adjustment processing are skin color conversion and color saturation. The human skin tone is a color that is typically remembered; viewers feel awkward when skin tone is converted to an unnatural color. This paper proposes as a solution a skin protection algorithm that detects human skin color tone and prevents skin color from changing. Moreover, the paper introduces an adaptive quadratic curve that reproduces natural appearances more vividly without color saturation. In addition, the system does not use field-to-field processing but pixel-to-pixel processing in real time so that incoming image display color can be controlled without interference from neighboring pixels.

articleTitle: A Globally Converging Blind Carrier Phase Offset Recovery Scheme for 8-VSB Signals
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a decision directed blind adaptive algorithm for carrier phase offset recovery of 8-VSB. The algorithm achieves phase recovery by minimizing the quadrature leakage into the in-phase component and removes undesirable local minima, which occur in most blind algorithms, by configuring the reliable leakage estimation region.

articleTitle: Enabling Legacy PTP Cameras and Printers as Networked PTP/IP Appliances
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: PTP/IP is a new connectivity standard for networked imaging appliances which combines the ease of use and seamless connectivity of picture transfer protocol (PTP) with the ubiquity of TCP/IP networks. In this paper we examine methods to allow legacy PTP appliances to gain the benefits of PTP/IP through the design of bridge and gateway adapters which can be simply plugged into the USB ports of such appliances. The internal firmware stacks of such adapters are described and practical case studies describe the adaption of legacy PTP cameras and printers to connect over a conventional 802.11 wireless LAN.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-efficient Display Controller for Low Power Devices in Presence of Occlusion
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Traditional image composition for output display involves accessing discrete overlay images and blending them together as per the requirement of the application. Increased display sizes and number of overlays increases the memory bandwidth. For low power SOCs with integrated display controllers display traffic has an adverse effect on the application's performance and power consumption. Based on the overlay positions and blending method used for output image composition only one overlay may occlude another fully or partially. Hardware display accelerators can take advantage of such occlusion to reduce memory bandwidth without compromising image quality. This paper presents strategies for such reduction for some of the popular blending algorithms. A bandwidth efficiency metric n is defined and is evaluated for each of the presented schemes. Savings in memory bandwidth leads to higher performance of applications and also reduced power at the memory interface and hence increasing battery lifetime.

articleTitle: Methods to Improve the Sound Reproduction of Limited Size Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Three examples will be given to improve sound reproduction, which all have 'distortion' in common. First, we push a loudspeaker to its limits. In the second example we add some distortion. In the third example we create a very high distortion level by replacing the original signal with another.

articleTitle: A PAPR Reduction Scheme using Time- and Frequency-Domain Clippings and its Performance Evaluation in a DVB-T System
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a suboptimal peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction scheme, which is based on the time- and frequency-domain clippings, and presents its performance evaluation results for the European standard for terrestrial digital video broadcast (DVB-T) system.

articleTitle: Deriving the Virtual World from Wireless Sensor Networks for Interaction with Consumer Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: By deploying wireless sensor networks in the future ubiquitous computing environment, smart consumer electronic devices could cooperate with such networks for sensing the environment and reacting upon various events more actively and accurately. However, the information gathered by sensor nodes may vary in locations and sensory devices, and is represented usually in complex form difficult to understand in the human side. In this study, we aim at constructing the virtual world where virtual objects visualize the information gathered in wireless sensor networks. The resulting virtual world may let users understand and estimate more easily the state of the real world measured by sensor networks, and interact with or through their consumer electronic devices.

articleTitle: Pilot-Aided Iterative Frequency Offset Estimation for Digital Video Broadcasting Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper deals with a simple way of estimating the integer frequency offset (IFO) of OFDM-based digital video broadcasting (DVB) system. By modifying the conventional maximum likelihood (ML) estimator to have multi-stage estimation strategy, the IFO estimator is derived. Simulations indicate that the proposed IFO estimator works robustly when compared to ML estimator.

articleTitle: Multi-carrier Optimization for Compressed Video Streaming
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we propose an optimization method to assign the modulator to each sub-carrier in the OFDM context. We solved the optimization problem using evolutionary programming, a faster solution in comparison to other techniques like dynamic programming. By exploiting the significance of video coded syntax elements, we also show that a joint source coding and transmission design increases the overall communication performance. The experimental results clearly show the advantageous of the two proposed solutions mentioned above.

articleTitle: A Robust Mobile-based Music Information Retrieval System
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a robust mobile-based music information retrieval (MIR) system. In the real mobile environment, a query music signal is captured by a cellular phone. A major problem in this environment is distortions contained in the features of the query sound due to the mobile network and environmental noise. In order to minimize the effect of these noises and so improve the system performance, we adopt a simple MA (moving average) filter which has relatively simple structure and low computational complexity. Then a SFS (sequential forward selection) feature optimization method is implemented to further improve and stabilize the system performance. The proposed system has been tested with cellular phones in the real world and it shows about 68% of average retrieving success rate. We include experimental results under the real world mobile environments.

articleTitle: Digital Broadcasting Contents Packaging for Storage Media
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a package format which binds digital broadcasts with related data such as TV-anytime metadata, additional resources, and usage history to store and reuse them. To achieve that, we adopt MPEG-4 file format as a container and apply a binary format for scenes (BIFS) for representing usage history. In addition, TV-anytime metadata is used to describe broadcasts and to provide the additional resources, e.g., mp3s, jpeg images, as well. To verify the usefulness of the proposed format, we introduce an application scenario and test it on the scenario.

articleTitle: An Efficient Implementation of Motion Estimation with Weight Prediction for ITU-T H.264 | MPEG-4 AVC
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: ITU-T H.264 | MPEG-4 AVC includes weight prediction in inter prediction process to improve coding efficiency when encoding video with a fading scene. Weight prediction, however, increases complexity of motion estimation (ME) process significantly in terms of additional operations and extra memory requirement. AVC performs weight prediction by scaling pixel value of the reference block to match with the fading effect. To follow this approach in ME, scaling operation has to be done at every pixel of all search blocks or precalculated before encoding. This paper proposes an efficient implementation method of weight prediction by scaling pixel value of the current block with an inverse of the weight factor instead. The proposed method reduces both the number of operations and memory requirement while sacrificing a negligible loss due to rounding error.

articleTitle: Development of T-DMB Receiver with CDMA Module for Interactive Data Broadcasting Services
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present the architecture of the interactive T-DMB receiver with a CDMA module for new services linked with the telecommunication network. After implemented it as hardware and software, we verify it by the interactive data service through the T-DMB and the CDMA network. This shows the possibilities of new interactive services in the digital broadcasting by utilizing the mobility of T-DMB and CDMA.

articleTitle: Refinements in Adaptive Quantization for Images Using the New Universal Quality Index
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper expands new research in adaptive DCT quantization for images using perceptual distortion control and the newly defined universal quality index with the goal of reducing blocking artifacts at low bit-rates. Results obtained show that this method converges and it does not need carefully calibrated viewing conditions.

articleTitle: A Simple Transcoding Algorithm for Streaming Service over Time-varying Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new transcoding algorithm that inserts an instantaneous decoding refresh (IDR) picture in any group of pictures (GOP). In the proposed algorithm, the transcoding process is carried out only within a single GOP instead of re-encoding the whole sequence. Furthermore, the experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm is superior to conventional method in terms of compression ratio.

articleTitle: Adaptive Algorithms to Improve Optical Disc Drive Robustness in Recording And Playback
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a couple of algorithms which can be used to correct the blank disc error through recording and playback performance improvement through disc error determination and correction on the fly during playing. These algorithms will not only greatly improve optical disc drive's recording quality over disc error but also playback robustness over wide disc quality variations.

articleTitle: Motion Vector Analysis Algorithm for Selective and Robust Digital Image Stabilization
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a precise and robust digital image stabilization system that uses motion vector analysis algorithm and selectively homography H based image warping under highly zoom-in camera. The proposed system removes not only the translational but also the distorted motion disturbances.

articleTitle: A Protocol-Based Contention Window for MBOA MAC
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In the early days of UWB development, IEEE802.15.3 MAC was a leading standard for UWB PHY, but now MBOA MAC has been considered as one of the most potential solutions for the medium access control (MAC) of the next generation of UWB PHY. Future home network may require that the MBOA MAC support a multi-protocol solution that will provide a mixed operation among PC, CE and mobile devices at the same time. Each device employs its own proper protocol. For example, AV devices for CE may use IEEE1394 protocol and mobile devices may use Bluetooth (BT) protocol. In order to support such multi-protocol environment effectively, the MBOA MAC needs to use a medium access method through a contention based on application protocol types. In this paper, we concentrate on defining a protocol-based contention window for a new medium access method. The values of protocol-based contention windows are determined by priority of application protocols.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of DMBonIP Gateway to Provide Internet Based DMB Service
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents DMBonIP gateway which can provide RTP/SDP based Internet streaming service by generating media streams in real time from the DMB ensemble received from the air. With DMBonIP gateway, DMB service area can be extended greatly without installing gap-fillers.

articleTitle: Directional diversity reception for ATSC 8VSB
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a reception improvement method for ATSC 8VSB in severe multipath channel using directional diversity. By applying directional diversity, we can eliminate undesired multipaths, so improve 8VSB reception performance. We demonstrate the performance of proposed method under severe multipath channel and show it can improve the reception of 8VSB system.

articleTitle: Image Authentication System Based on Two-Dimensional Matrix Codes Without Contamination of Original Images
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes an authentication system without contamination of original images. The proposed system also realizes complete reconstruction of original signatures by introduction of 2-D matrix codes including error correction capability. Therefore, the system is suitable for the recent digital rights management.

articleTitle: An Advanced Fast Channel Tracking Method for Automotive Digital TV Receiver
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, an advanced fast channel tracking method is proposed for automotive DTV receiver. The auto channel tracking function tunes an alternative broadcaster which belongs to affiliation group automatically, when channel condition is getting worse. Auto channel tracking is a practical approach to support comfortable reception. The proposed method substantially improves the channel tracking speed. The advantage of the proposed method is confirmed by an experiment.

articleTitle: Amplitude-DQPSK Modulation for High-Data-Rate Terrestrial Digital Multimedia Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Amplitude-DQPSK modulation method is proposed for a high-data-rate T-DMB system with the backward compatibility to existing receivers. Simulation results show that the proposed A-DQPSK can be a good choice to achieve high-data rate over other possible modulation schemes.

articleTitle: On-Line Musical Beat Tracking with Phase-Locked-Loop (PLL) Techniique
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An on-line beat tracking algorithm based on the digital phase-locked-loop (PLL) technique is proposed in this work, which estimates both the music tempo and the position of beat pulses in real time. In addition to a detailed description of the proposed algorithm, we show that the PLL-technique is effective in its tracking performance and simple to implement.

articleTitle: DVB-T Receiver With a Fully Digital I/Q Separator
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes the design of a digital I/Q separator which is applied to DVB-T receivers. The proposed I/Q separator not only avoids problems caused by analog I/Q separators, e.g., gain error, phase error, DC offset, etc., it also resolves the difficulties of prior digital I/Q separators, e.g., large area, large gate count, and high power consumption by insertion of decimation filters. A prototypical system as well as a chip has been designed using 0.18-mum single-poly six-metal CMOS process with core area of 1.59 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The total power consumption is merely 433 muW at a 20.0 MHz system clock.

articleTitle: Adaptive Hypermedia Searches for Mobile PDA
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper focuses on devising a new search mechanism, called an adaptive hypermedia search, which utilizes hierarchical structure of hypermedia objects within a given e-learning service domain for mobile PDA device which has usually limited resources. Hyperlinked contents can be theoretically represented as graphs to generate hyperlinked objects for more convenient and effective searching of relevant contents. A mathematical model is developed to structure hyperlinked objects optimally so that most relevant contents can be reachable more efficiently with the optimal-structured content objects. We developed a tree-filtering algorithm and a top k algorithm that can be used to provide search recommendations for mobile PDA systems.

articleTitle: Automatic Chapter Generation for Consumer Videos
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for automatic chapter generation of consumer videos, in which the knowledge of media aesthetics and video production is utilized. For an input video, a set of specific visual and aural aesthetic features, called expressive elements, is first extracted. Then a high-level structure with aesthetic semantics, namely aesthetic intensity, is obtained and used to generate the corresponding video chapters. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: EXT3NS: Multimedia File System Supporting Network/Storage Card
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The EXT3NS is a file system based on a special HIW device, called NS card for multimedia data. In general, normal computer has high level of CPU utilization for networking operations with gigabit level and several copy operations. Therefore, we have developed the NS card to alleviate this overhead. EXT3NS provides the standard API's to read and write files in storage unit of NS card. The performance measurements on our system show obvious performance improvements. Especially, the system shows much less server's CPU utilization and less fluctuation of client bitrate, hence more reliable streaming service is possible.

articleTitle: A DS UWB Wireless Medical System
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present an DS UWB wireless medical system with transmission power assignment mechanism. An essential feature of this system is that higher power is allocated to the medical information that requires higher quality of service. To achieve the purpose of maximum resource utilization, or minimum total transmission power, we also incorporate a orthogonal variable spreading factor codes (OVSF) strategy, and unequal error protection mechanism into the proposed power control scheme. Specifically, we employ high power, high level error protection mechanism, and the long OVSF code for medical messages that dictate stringent bit error rate (BER). In contrast, low power, low level error protection mechanism, and short OVSF code are granted to messages that can tolerate high BER. For a practical wireless communication scenario, a simulation has been carried out to verify proper functioning of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Frame Accurate Editing in Blu-ray MPEG-2 Transport Streams
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Video editing in DVD recorders today is GOP accurate. However with the advent of the Blu-ray recorders and HDTVs, the incorrect frames present in GOP accurate editing become easily identifiable. This paper discusses a very convenient and computationally undemanding way to achieve frame accurate editing on Blu-ray streams.

articleTitle: Personalized Audio Broadcasting System through the Terrestrial- DMB System
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes the personalized audio broadcasting services through the terrestrial digital multimedia broadcasting (T-DMB) system. This system consists of preprocessing module, authoring module, T-DMB transmission/reception module and playing terminal. Through this system user can control the 3D audio scene freely or choose the preset 3D audio scene. This system can be applied to DMB, 3DTV and home shopping applications to provide interactivity and realistic feelings.

articleTitle: Jointly Reducing The Quality/Bitrate Fluctuations in Mixed Motion Sequences in the H. 264 Video Coding Standard
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper illustrates a novel mechanism which jointly reduces PSNR and rate variations in the H.264 video coding standard in mixed motion scenes. Our scheme exploits a simple binary search combined with dynamic cut scene and fade identifiers. Results show 24% less variance on PSNR and 93% less variance on rate. Furthermore it reduces the percentage of dropped frames to almost zero while achieving near constant and on target bit and frame rates.

articleTitle: An Edge-Based 3D Y/C Separation Using Wavelet Transform and Motion Compensation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a new 3D adaptive Y/C separation algorithm for the composite video signal decoding. The proposed algorithm has an adaptive architecture with which multiplication coefficients are adjusted by the similarity values between two pixels in lines of a field, two consecutive fields, and two consecutive frames.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Ethernet/High-speed Power Line Communication Bridge Supporting QoS
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The QoS support is very important for the future home network services. Since home network is mixed with various types of networks, it is required to support QoS even when traffics flow over non-QoS network like Ethernet. We design and implement a bridge system providing QoS which connects non-QoS and QoS networks, more specifically Ethernet and high-speed power line communication (H-PLC). This paper explains the issues for supporting QoS and introduces a QoS bridge system for Ethernet and H-PLC.

articleTitle: Design of Gateway Architecture for Real-Time A/V Streaming between IEEE1394 Network And Ethernet
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents design architecture for multimedia streaming gateway to transfer audio/video (A/V) contents between IEEE1394 network and Ethernet. In IEEE 1394 network, digital video (DV) is the de-facto standard streaming format, and MPEG4 is a well-known streaming format used in Ethernet based network. A hardware and software co-designed architecture is suggested to support the real-time transcoding between IEEE 1394 based DV and Ethernet based MPEG4 streaming in this paper. And a prototype was implemented to verify the performance of the transcoder service in multiprotocol based home network environment.

articleTitle: Frequency Synchronization Technique for The Equalization Digital On-Channel Repeater in ATSC system
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a frequency synchronization technique for the equalization digital on-channel repeater (EDOCR) in ATSC system is proposed and the proposed algorithm is verified by mathematical analysis. The proposed algorithm uses the frequency offset information that comes from carrier and symbol timing recovery in the receiving part of EDOCR when the demodulated symbol is re-modulated in transmitting part. Therefore, the algorithm makes it possible for the EDOCR output signal to synchronize with input signal in frequency without additional reference source. Also, the synchronized EDOCR output does not degrade the reception performance of legacy receivers.

articleTitle: From CD to DVD and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Recording the information is a habit that goes back in time about 100,000 years, when humans produced apparently their first ornaments. Many global changes have taken places since then and have affected the way we handle the analog and later the digital information. The CD and DVD represent exponents of wonderful technologies we experience daily, but where is optical storage heading to? Will the DVD be replaced? Will holographic storage prevail? We might have some of the answers, but questions like these keep inevitably recurring.

articleTitle: Seamless Viewpoint Switching for Multiview Video
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a smooth viewpoint change scheme for multiview video using view interpolation based on image warping techniques. The proposed method produces high-quality scenes for continuously changing viewpoints and needs only cost-effective coding overheads. The proposed scheme facilitates seamless viewpoint-aware video playback and provides a new experience for video entertainments, like sports or performance.

articleTitle: VisualEPG: Informing the TV Experience with Web Metadata
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Video can increasingly be watched from Internet streamed, downloaded and recorded sources in addition to live broadcast television. The quantity and heterogeneity of these often long-tail video sources are likely to spur the creation of new methods to browse and consume video. In addition, as television advertising moves closer to the Web model of targeted advertising, an interactive television experience that integrates both kinds of content in an open way is required. In particular, users can now move between watching video and browsing the Web. These two media experiences can be made synergistic if we think of Web content as informing the video experience and vice versa. We illustrate this idea with a system for browsing live HDTV based on Web metadata and suggest it as a basis for a combined system for viewing both diverse video sources and related Web content.

articleTitle: A Scheduling Algorithm for Supporting Multimedia Traffic in IEEE 802.11e Wireless Home Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a smart scheduling algorithm (S2A) for supporting multimedia traffic in IEEE 802.11e HCCA. Based on the accurate traffic prediction, S2A allocates transmission opportunity (TXOP) for each flow efficiently, and computes optimal service interval (SI). Preliminary evaluations showed that the predictions on the next VBR frame size and its expected arrival time at AP are very accurate. Thus, we expect that S2A can fully utilize the actual traffic characteristics for the efficient TXOP allocation and SI computation.

articleTitle: Efficient Carrier Recovery for High-Order QAM
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of Technical Papers International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A novel carrier recovery algorithm for high-order quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) is proposed in this paper. Besides the traditional decision-directed phase detector, the algorithm employs an improved polarity-based phase detector to extend the acquisition range of carrier frequency offset. And when combined with a dual-mode adaptive equalization algorithm, it can be used in the application over multi-path channels. Simulation results demonstrate that it can deal with carrier frequency offset up to 960kHz@256QAM over AWGN channels and 690kHz@256QAM over typical coaxial cable channels at a baud rate of 6.9Msps. Meanwhile, its complexity is quite low.
